spec.api: API Gateway WebSockets accepts joins, hand raises, and questions. A REST endpoint creates each office-hours session.
spec.processing: Lambda validates actions and publishes queue changes to connected students. EventBridge closes the session and starts recap generation.
spec.storage: DynamoDB stores session metadata, questions, answers, and active connections. S3 stores a durable recap.
spec.bottlenecks: Connection spikes are isolated by session. Writes use conditional updates so two hand raises cannot take the same queue position.

spec.api: Students connect through WebSockets while mentors use a small REST dashboard to start, pause, and answer questions.
spec.processing: A session service appends questions to a FIFO queue and broadcasts state snapshots. A scheduled worker closes sessions and emits a recap event.
spec.storage: DynamoDB keeps the live session state and answer history. S3 retains session recap artifacts for later learning.
spec.bottlenecks: The queue is partitioned by session. A connection registry is pruned on disconnect so fan-out does not repeatedly target stale clients.

spec.api: Students submit a demo link and structured feedback through a REST API. The UI receives status updates by polling a lightweight feed.
spec.processing: Lambda stores the demo, then sends reviewer-matching work through SQS. A worker chooses a small reviewer set and records invitations.
spec.storage: DynamoDB stores demos, feedback tags, reviewer state, and delivery idempotency keys. S3 stores optional thumbnails.
spec.bottlenecks: The queue absorbs a workshop burst. Idempotency keys prevent duplicate feedback when a student retries after a weak connection.

tweakNote: Swapped DynamoDB Streams fan-out for Redis Pub/Sub to cut late-joiner latency under load.

spec.api: Same WebSocket join/question path, but the gateway also publishes a lightweight presence ping so the connection registry stays accurate for fan-out.
spec.processing: The session Lambda now writes queue changes once and publishes them through Redis Pub/Sub. Each connected node receives the delta and pushes it to its own sockets, so a 500-student session fans out without re-reading DynamoDB.
spec.storage: DynamoDB remains the source of truth for session state and recaps; Redis holds only the ephemeral live channel. S3 still stores the durable recap.
spec.bottlenecks: Redis replaces the stream poll so a late joiner gets the current state in one cached read. If Redis drops, the system falls back to the DynamoDB snapshot rather than losing the session.
